at hacke.explanation: "At hacke" means "to hack", as in breaking into a computer. Do not mix it up with "at hakke" (to chop), which has two k: "Jeg hakker løg" (I chop onions).

sentence.da: Nogen forsøgte at **hacke** firmaets netværk i går nat.
sentence.en: Someone tried to hack the company's network last night.

at hade.explanation: "At hade" means "to hate". It is a strong word. For a mild dislike, use "kan ikke lide" (do not like): "Jeg kan ikke lide kaffe" (I do not like coffee).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **hade** andre.
sentence.en: You should not hate others.

at hagle.explanation: "At hagle" means "to hail", as in ice falling from the sky. This verb must be used with "det" (it): "Det hagler" (It is hailing).

sentence.da: Det begynder at **hagle** med store, hårde isklumper.
sentence.en: It starts to hail with big, hard lumps of ice.

at hakke.explanation: "At hakke" means "to chop". A very common word partner is "kød" (meat): "hakket kød" (minced meat).

sentence.da: Man kan **hakke** persille med en skarp kniv.
sentence.en: You can chop parsley with a sharp knife.

at halte.explanation: "At halte" means "to limp". To say an argument has a flaw, it is also used: "Argumentet halter" (The argument is flawed).

sentence.da: Han vil **halte** i flere uger, fordi hans fod er brækket.
sentence.en: He will limp for several weeks because his foot is broken.

at halvere.explanation: "At halvere" means "to halve". It is built from "halv" (half) and the verb ending "-ere". To say an amount was cut in half: "Antallet blev halveret" (The number was halved).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **halvere** prisen på alle varer.
sentence.en: The store will halve the price of all goods.

at handle.explanation: "At handle" means "to shop or to act". To say you buy things in stores: "Jeg handler i supermarkedet" (I shop at the supermarket). To say someone must take action: "Vi må handle nu" (We must act now).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **handle** i den nye butik.
sentence.en: I want to shop in the new store.

at handle ind.explanation: "At handle ind" means "to go grocery shopping". It is built from "at handle" (to shop) and "ind" (in). For clothes, use "at shoppe" (to shop) instead: "Jeg shopper tøj i byen" (I shop for clothes in town).

sentence.da: Vi skal **handle ind**, fordi der ikke er mælk.
sentence.en: We have to go grocery shopping because there is no milk.

at handle om.explanation: "At handle om" means "to be about". To say what a conversation is about: "Samtalen handlede om penge" (The conversation was about money). Do not mix it up with "at handle" (to shop): "Jeg handler i supermarkedet" (I shop at the supermarket).

sentence.da: Min bog skal **handle om** en hund.
sentence.en: My book is going to be about a dog.

at harmonere.explanation: "At harmonere" means "to harmonize". To say what it goes with, add "med" (with): "Gardinerne harmonerer med væggene" (The curtains go well with the walls).

sentence.da: Gule og blå farver kan **harmonere** godt.
sentence.en: Yellow and blue colors can harmonize well.

at have.explanation: "At have" means "to have". To talk about the past, use "har" (have) with another verb: "Jeg har spist" (I have eaten). To say it is your birthday: "Jeg har fødselsdag" (literally, "I have birthday").

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have** en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like to have a cup of coffee.

at have ansvar for.explanation: "At have ansvar for" means "to be responsible for". "Ansvar" means "responsibility", so it is literally "to have responsibility for". To ask who is in charge of a task: "Hvem har ansvar for opvasken?" (Who is responsible for the dishes?)

sentence.da: Læreren skal **have ansvar for** klassen.
sentence.en: The teacher has to be responsible for the class.

at have brug for.explanation: "At have brug for" means "to need". Literally, it is "to have use for". To say you do not need to do something, use "at behøve" (to need) with "ikke" (not): "Du behøver ikke at komme" (You do not need to come).

sentence.da: Man kan **have brug for** en paraply.
sentence.en: You may need an umbrella.

at have det sjovt.explanation: "At have det sjovt" means "to have fun". The part "have det" (to feel) works with other feelings too: "Jeg har det godt" (I feel good).

sentence.da: Vi vil **have det sjovt** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to have fun this weekend.

at have en finger med i spillet.explanation: "At have en finger med i spillet" means "to be involved". Literally, it is "to have a finger in the game". To say you are not involved: "Jeg har ikke en finger med i spillet" (I am not involved).

forms.da: Han har en finger med i spillet
Hun havde en finger med i spillet
forms.en: She had a hand in it

forms.da: Har du en finger med i spillet?

sentence.da: Politiet tror, at flere kan **have en finger med i spillet**.
sentence.en: The police think that several people may be involved.

at have en høne at plukke med nogen.explanation: "At have en høne at plukke med nogen" means "to have a bone to pick with someone". Literally, it is "to have a hen to pluck with someone". To say who it is, end with "med" (with) and that person: "Han har en høne at plukke med naboen" (He has a bone to pick with the neighbor).

forms.da: Jeg har en høne at plukke med dig
forms.en: I have a bone to pick with you

forms.da: Har du en høne at plukke med ham?
forms.en: Do you have a bone to pick with him?

forms.da: Hun havde en høne at plukke med sin bror
forms.en: She had a bone to pick with her brother

sentence.da: Det er svært at **have en høne at plukke med nogen**, man holder af.
sentence.en: It is hard to have a bone to pick with someone you love.

at have fri.explanation: "At have fri" means "to be off work". The same words work for school: "Børnene har fri i dag" (The children are off today). To say you take a day off, use "at holde fri" (to take time off): "Jeg holder fri på fredag" (I am taking Friday off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have fri** på mandag.
sentence.en: I would like to have Monday off.

at have fødselsdag.explanation: "At have fødselsdag" means "to have a birthday", and it is how you say it is your birthday: "Jeg har fødselsdag i dag" (It is my birthday today). To congratulate someone, say "Tillykke med fødselsdagen!" (Happy birthday!).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **have fødselsdag** i morgen.
sentence.en: My brother has his birthday tomorrow.

at have god tid.explanation: "At have god tid" means "to have plenty of time". To say you are busy, use "at have travlt" (to be busy): "Jeg har travlt i dag" (I am busy today).

forms.en: I have had plenty of time

sentence.da: Vi skal tage afsted tidligt for at **have god tid**.
sentence.en: We have to leave early to have plenty of time.

at have hjertet på rette sted.explanation: "At have hjertet på rette sted" means "to have one's heart in the right place". To admit a flaw and still say the person means well, add "men" (but): "Han er sur, men han har hjertet på rette sted" (He is grumpy, but his heart is in the right place).

forms.da: Han har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: He has his heart in the right place.

forms.da: Hun er klodset, men hun har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: She is clumsy, but her heart is in the right place.

forms.da: Jeg ved, at du har hjertet på rette sted.
forms.en: I know your heart is in the right place.

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **have hjertet på rette sted**, når man hjælper andre.
sentence.en: It is important to have your heart in the right place when you help others.

at have is i maven.explanation: "At have is i maven" means "to stay calm". Literally, it is "to have ice in the stomach". To give advice: "Man skal have is i maven" (You have to keep your cool).

sentence.da: Før eksamen er det vigtigt at **have is i maven**.
sentence.en: Before the exam it is important to keep your cool.

at have let ved.explanation: "At have let ved" means "to find it easy to". To name the activity you find easy, add "at" (to) and a verb after "ved" (at): "Jeg har let ved at lære sprog" (I find it easy to learn languages). For the opposite, use "at have svært ved" (to find it hard to): "Jeg har svært ved at stå op" (I find it hard to get up).

forms.en: I have found it easy to

sentence.da: Han kan **have let ved** at tegne, fordi han øver sig meget.
sentence.en: He can find it easy to draw because he practices a lot.

at have lyst til.explanation: "At have lyst til" means "to feel like or want to". To name what you feel like having: "Jeg har lyst til kaffe" (I feel like coffee). To name an activity, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg har lyst til at gå en tur" (I feel like going for a walk).

forms.en: I have felt like / wanted to

sentence.da: Man kan **have lyst til** en kold drink, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: You can feel like a cold drink when it is hot.

at have mulighed for.explanation: "At have mulighed for" means "to have the opportunity to". For a simple "can", use "kan" (can) instead: "Jeg kan komme" (I can come).

forms.en: I have had the opportunity to

sentence.da: Du skal **have mulighed for** at tale med chefen.
sentence.en: You should have the chance to talk to the boss.

at have noget imod.explanation: "At have noget imod" means "to mind or object to". To ask if something bothers someone: "Har du noget imod, at jeg åbner vinduet?" (Do you mind if I open the window?) To say it does not bother you: "Jeg har ikke noget imod det" (I do not mind that).

sentence.da: Jeg ville ikke **have noget imod** en kop te.
sentence.en: I would not mind a cup of tea.

at have ondt i.explanation: "At have ondt i" means "to have a pain in". To say your head hurts: "Jeg har ondt i hovedet" (I have a headache). Danish says "hovedet" (the head) where English says "my head".

forms.en: I have had a pain in

sentence.da: Efter koncerten kan man **have ondt i** halsen.
sentence.en: After the concert, you can have a sore throat.

at have på.explanation: "At have på" means "to wear", literally "to have on". To say you put on a piece of clothing, use "at tage på" (to put on): "Jeg tager jakken på" (I put my jacket on).

sentence.da: Hvad skal du **have på** i aften?
sentence.en: What are you going to wear tonight?

at have ret.explanation: "At have ret" means "to be right". Literally, Danish says "to have right": "Du har ret" (You are right). When you add "til" (to), it means an official right: "Du har ret til ferie" (You have the right to vacation).

sentence.da: Ja, du kan **have ret** i det.
sentence.en: Yes, you may be right about that.

at have råd til.explanation: "At have råd til" means "to afford". To say you cannot buy something: "Jeg har ikke råd til en ny telefon" (I cannot afford a new phone). Do not mix it up with "et råd" (a piece of advice): "Jeg giver dig et råd" (I give you a piece of advice).

forms.en: I have been able to afford

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **have råd til** en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I would like to be able to afford a new bike.

at have svært ved.explanation: "At have svært ved" means "to find it hard to". To name the activity you find hard, add "at" (to) and a verb after "ved" (at): "Jeg har svært ved at sove" (I find it hard to sleep). You can also name a school subject directly after "ved": "Hun har svært ved matematik" (She finds math hard).

forms.en: I have found it hard to

sentence.da: Jeg kan **have svært ved** at stå tidligt op.
sentence.en: I can find it hard to get up early.

at have tid til.explanation: "At have tid til" means "to have time for". To ask if someone is free for something: "Har du tid til en kop kaffe?" (Do you have time for a cup of coffee?) To name an activity, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg har tid til at læse" (I have time to read).

sentence.da: Efter arbejde vil jeg **have tid til** børnene.
sentence.en: After work, I want to have time for the children.

at have travlt.explanation: "At have travlt" means "to be busy". Literally, it is "to have busy". To say you are in a hurry, the same words work: "Jeg har travlt, bussen kører snart" (I am in a hurry, the bus leaves soon).

sentence.da: Før jul kan butikkerne **have travlt**.
sentence.en: Before Christmas the stores can be busy.

at havne.explanation: "At havne" means "to end up". To say where a ball finished: "Bolden havnede i søen" (The ball ended up in the lake). It comes from "en havn" (a harbor).

sentence.da: Pakken kan **havne** hos naboen, hvis vi ikke er hjemme.
sentence.en: The package may end up at the neighbor's if we are not home.

at hedde.explanation: "At hedde" means "to be called", and it is how you give your name: "Jeg hedder Anna" means "My name is Anna". It is also used for things: "Hvad hedder det på dansk?" (What is that called in Danish?).

sentence.da: Vores nye hund skal **hedde** Max.
sentence.en: Our new dog is going to be called Max.

at helbrede.explanation: "At helbrede" means "to cure or heal". To say a medicine makes an illness go away: "Medicinen helbredte sygdommen" (The medicine cured the illness). When a scrape closes by itself, use "at hele" (to heal): "Skrammen heler hurtigt" (The scrape heals quickly).

sentence.da: Man kan **helbrede** nogle sygdomme med den rigtige behandling.
sentence.en: Some illnesses can be cured with the right treatment.

at hele.explanation: "At hele" means "to heal". To say a scrape closes over time: "Skrammen heler hurtigt" (The scrape heals quickly). When a doctor makes an illness go away, use "at helbrede" (to cure): "Lægen helbredte patienten" (The doctor cured the patient).

sentence.da: Et brækket ben kan **hele** på seks uger.
sentence.en: A broken leg can heal in six weeks.

at henrette.explanation: "At henrette" means "to execute", as in killing someone as an official punishment. For any other killing, use "at dræbe" (to kill): "Han dræbte en mand" (He killed a man).

sentence.da: I nogle lande kan staten stadig **henrette** forbrydere.
sentence.en: In some countries the state can still execute criminals.

at hente.explanation: "At hente" means "to fetch or pick up". To say you collect a parcel: "Jeg henter pakken på posthuset" (I am picking up the parcel at the post office). To get something that is simply given to you, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg får en gave" (I get a present).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hente** børnene i skolen klokken tre.
sentence.en: I have to pick up the children at school at three o'clock.

at henvende sig.explanation: "At henvende sig" means "to contact or turn to". To name who you turn to, add "til" (to): "Jeg henvendte mig til kommunen" (I contacted the municipality). To tell someone where to go: "Henvend dig i receptionen" (Please go to the reception desk).

sentence.da: Man kan **henvende sig** til biblioteket, hvis man har spørgsmål.
sentence.en: You can turn to the library if you have questions.

at henvise.explanation: "At henvise" means "to refer". To send someone on to a place, use "til" (to): "Receptionen henviste mig til første sal" (The reception sent me to the first floor). To point to a source in a text: "Teksten henviser til en bog" (The text refers to a book).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **henvise** mig til en specialist på sygehuset.
sentence.en: The doctor will refer me to a specialist at the hospital.

at heppe.explanation: "At heppe" means "to cheer (for a team)". To name who you cheer for, use "på" (for) after it: "Vi hepper på Danmark" (We are cheering for Denmark).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **heppe** på dig, når du løber maraton.
sentence.en: I will cheer for you when you run the marathon.

at hikke.explanation: "At hikke" means "to hiccup". The noun is "et hik" (a hiccup). To say you cannot stop: "Jeg hikker hele tiden" (I am hiccuping all the time).

sentence.da: Man begynder at **hikke**, når man drikker for hurtigt.
sentence.en: You start to hiccup when you drink too fast.

at hilse.explanation: "At hilse" means "to greet or say hello". To pass on a hello from someone: "Hils ham fra mig!" (Say hi to him from me!) To say hello to a person you meet, use "at hilse på" (to say hello to): "Jeg hilser på naboen" (I say hello to the neighbor).

sentence.da: Man skal **hilse**, når man kommer ind i butikken.
sentence.en: You should say hello when you walk into the store.

at hilse på.explanation: "At hilse på" means "to say hello to or meet". To say you want to meet someone: "Jeg vil gerne hilse på din mor" (I would like to meet your mom). To pass on a hello, use "at hilse" (to greet): "Hils din mor fra mig" (Say hi to your mom from me).

forms.en: I have said hello to / met

sentence.da: Du skal **hilse på** gæsterne, når de kommer.
sentence.en: You have to greet the guests when they arrive.

at hindre.explanation: "At hindre" means "to prevent or hinder". To name the action that is stopped, use "i at" (from) and a verb: "Sneen hindrede os i at køre" (The snow kept us from driving).

sentence.da: Et væltet træ kan **hindre** trafikken på landevejen.
sentence.en: A fallen tree can hinder traffic on the country road.

at hive.explanation: "At hive" means "to pull or heave". To say you tug at something, add "i" (at): "Barnet hiver i min jakke" (The child tugs at my jacket). To say you gasp for breath, use "at hive efter vejret": "Han hev efter vejret" (He gasped for breath).

sentence.da: Fiskeren skal **hive** nettet op af vandet med begge hænder.
sentence.en: The fisherman has to pull the net out of the water with both hands.

at hjælpe.explanation: "At hjælpe" means "to help". To offer help in a shop: "Kan jeg hjælpe dig?" (Can I help you?) To call out in an emergency: "Hjælp!" (Help!)

sentence.da: Lægen vil **hjælpe** den syge mand.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to help the sick man.

at hjælpe med.explanation: "At hjælpe med" means "to help with". To name the task, put it after "med" (with): "Jeg hjælper med lektierne" (I help with the homework). To name the person you help, put that person before "med": "Jeg hjælper dig med maden" (I help you with the food).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **hjælpe med** flytningen.
sentence.en: My brother wants to help with the move.

at hjælpe til.explanation: "At hjælpe til" means "to help out". To say kids are helping at an event: "Børnene hjælper til ved festen" (The kids help out at the party). To say you help a particular person, leave out "til": "Jeg hjælper min mor" (I help my mom).

sentence.da: Vil du **hjælpe til** i køkkenet i aften?
sentence.en: Do you want to help out in the kitchen tonight?

at holde.explanation: "At holde" means "to hold or keep". To say you are holding something: "Hun holder en kop kaffe" (She is holding a cup of coffee). To say someone does what he promises: "Han holder, hvad han lover" (He keeps what he promises).

sentence.da: Kan du **holde** min taske et øjeblik?
sentence.en: Can you hold my bag for a moment?

at holde af.explanation: "At holde af" means "to be fond of". To name who you are fond of, put the person after "af" (of): "Jeg holder meget af min bedstemor" (I am very fond of my grandmother).

sentence.da: Man kan **holde af** en ven uden at elske ham.
sentence.en: You can be fond of a friend without loving him.

at holde et løfte.explanation: "At holde et løfte" means "to keep a promise". Danish uses "holde" (to hold) where English says "keep". To say you break a promise, use "at bryde et løfte" (to break a promise): "Han brød sit løfte" (He broke his promise).

sentence.da: Man skal altid **holde et løfte**.
sentence.en: You must always keep a promise.

at holde fast.explanation: "At holde fast" means "to hold on". To tell someone to grip something: "Hold fast i rælingen!" (Hold on to the railing!) To say someone sticks to an idea: "Han holder fast i sin mening" (He sticks to his opinion).

sentence.da: Du skal **holde fast**, når bussen kører.
sentence.en: You must hold on when the bus is moving.

at holde ferie.explanation: "At holde ferie" means "to be on vacation". To say you take just one day off, use "at tage fri" (to take a day off): "Jeg tager fri i morgen" (I am taking tomorrow off).

sentence.da: Vi vil **holde ferie** ved havet i år.
sentence.en: We want to be on vacation by the sea this year.

at holde fest.explanation: "At holde fest" means "to throw a party". To say you go to a party, use "at tage til fest" (to go to a party): "Han tager til fest" (He is going to a party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **holde fest** i haven på lørdag.
sentence.en: We want to throw a party in the garden on Saturday.

at holde fri.explanation: "At holde fri" means "to take time off". To say you are simply off work, use "at have fri" (to be off work): "Jeg har fri i dag" (I am off work today).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **holde fri**, fordi jeg skal til lægen.
sentence.en: I want to take time off because I am going to the doctor.

at holde i hånd.explanation: "At holde i hånd" means "to hold hands". Danish literally says "i hånd" (in hand), with just one "hånd" (hand), even though two people are involved. To say a couple walks holding hands: "De går og holder i hånd" (They walk holding hands).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **holde i hånd**, når de krydser vejen.
sentence.en: The children must hold hands when they cross the road.

at holde med.explanation: "At holde med" means "to support". To ask which team someone supports: "Hvem holder du med?" (Who do you support?) To name your own team: "Jeg holder med Brøndby" (I support Brøndby).

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **holde med** det danske hold.
sentence.en: I usually support the Danish team.

at holde møde.explanation: "At holde møde" means "to have a meeting". Danish uses "holde" (to hold) here, just as English can say "hold a meeting". To ask when it takes place: "Hvornår holder vi møde?" (When are we having a meeting?)

sentence.da: Vi skal **holde møde** i morgen tidlig.
sentence.en: We are having a meeting tomorrow morning.

at holde op.explanation: "At holde op" means "to stop". To say a noise stops: "Larmen holder op" (The noise stops). To name the activity you quit, add "med at" (with to) and a verb: "Hun holdt op med at synge" (She quit singing).

sentence.da: Musikken skal **holde op** klokken ti.
sentence.en: The music has to stop at ten o'clock.

at holde op med.explanation: "At holde op med" means "to stop doing". Without "med" (with), "holde op" means "to stop": "Regnen holder op" (The rain stops).

sentence.da: Du skal **holde op med** at råbe.
sentence.en: You have to stop yelling.

at holde oplæg.explanation: "At holde oplæg" means "to give a presentation". Danish uses "holde" (to hold) where English says "give". The same verb works for a speech: "at holde en tale" (to give a speech).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **holde oplæg** om mit projekt for hele klassen.
sentence.en: I am going to give a presentation about my project to the whole class.

at holde ord.explanation: "At holde ord" means "to keep one's word". Danish uses no word for "his" or "her" here: "Hun holder altid ord" (She always keeps her word).

sentence.da: Når du har lovet noget, skal du **holde ord**.
sentence.en: When you have promised something, you must keep your word.

at holde pause.explanation: "At holde pause" means "to take a break". Another way to say it is "at tage en pause" (to take a break): "Jeg tager en pause" (I am taking a break).

sentence.da: Vi skal **holde pause**, fordi vi er trætte.
sentence.en: We have to take a break because we are tired.

at holde sammen.explanation: "At holde sammen" means "to stick together". To say a family stays united: "Familien holder sammen" (The family sticks together). When you mean things that stay in one piece, the same verb is used: "Kagen holder ikke sammen" (The cake does not hold together).

sentence.da: I svære tider skal vi **holde sammen**.
sentence.en: In hard times, we must stick together.

at holde sig.explanation: "At holde sig" means "to keep or stay". To tell someone to stick to the subject: "Hold dig til sagen!" (Stick to the point!) To say you keep warm, add the state: "at holde sig varm" (to keep warm).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **holde sig** væk fra ilden.
sentence.en: The children must stay away from the fire.

at holde sig i form.explanation: "At holde sig i form" means "to stay in shape". "Sig" (oneself) changes with the person: "Du holder dig i form" (You stay in shape). To ask how someone stays fit: "Hvordan holder du dig i form?" (How do you stay in shape?)

forms.da: jeg har holdt mig i form

sentence.da: Man skal **holde sig i form**, når man bliver ældre.
sentence.en: You have to stay in shape as you get older.

at holde styr på.explanation: "At holde styr på" means "to keep track of". To say you keep track of your money: "Jeg holder styr på mine penge" (I keep track of my money). To watch over someone, use "at holde øje med" (to keep an eye on): "Jeg holder øje med børnene" (I am keeping an eye on the children).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **holde styr på** alle børnene.
sentence.en: It is hard to keep track of all the kids.

at holde tale.explanation: "At holde tale" means "to give a speech". Danish uses "holde" (to hold) where English says "give". To say who gave a speech at a wedding: "Brudens far holdt tale" (The bride's father gave a speech).

sentence.da: Min chef vil **holde tale** ved festen.
sentence.en: My boss wants to give a speech at the party.

at holde tand for tunge.explanation: "At holde tand for tunge" means "to keep quiet". Literally, it is "to hold tooth before tongue". To say someone kept a secret: "Hun holdt tand for tunge om gaven" (She kept quiet about the present).

sentence.da: Du må **holde tand for tunge** og ikke sige noget om gaven.
sentence.en: You must keep quiet and not say anything about the present.

at holde øje med.explanation: "At holde øje med" means "to keep an eye on". Literally, it is "to hold eye with". To ask someone to watch a child: "Hold øje med barnet!" (Keep an eye on the child!)

forms.en: I have kept an eye on

sentence.da: Kan du **holde øje med** min taske?
sentence.en: Can you keep an eye on my bag?

at hoppe.explanation: "At hoppe" means "to jump". To say you jump up onto something, add "op" (up): "Katten hopper op på bordet" (The cat jumps up onto the table).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **hoppe** i vandet.
sentence.en: The children want to jump into the water.

at hoste.explanation: "At hoste" means "to cough". To say you have been coughing for a while: "Jeg har hostet i tre dage" (I have been coughing for three days).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og må **hoste** hele natten.
sentence.en: I am sick and have to cough all night.

at hugge.explanation: "At hugge" means "to chop". To say you chop firewood: "Han hugger brænde" (He chops firewood). To cut with a knife, use "at skære" (to cut): "Jeg skærer brødet" (I cut the bread).

sentence.da: Man bruger en økse til at **hugge** træ.
sentence.en: You use an axe to chop wood.

at hulke.explanation: "At hulke" means "to sob". To say someone sobs hard: "Han hulkede i flere minutter" (He sobbed for several minutes). For ordinary crying, use "at græde" (to cry): "Barnet græder" (The child is crying).

sentence.da: Efter nyheden om ulykken begyndte hun at **hulke**.
sentence.en: After the news of the accident she began to sob.

at huske.explanation: "At huske" means "to remember". To remind someone to do something: "Husk at ringe" (Remember to call). To keep a fact in mind, use "at huske på" (to keep in mind): "Husk på, at det er farligt" (Keep in mind that it is dangerous).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **huske** hans navn.
sentence.en: I can't remember his name.

at huske på.explanation: "At huske på" means "to keep in mind". To tell someone to bear a fact in mind: "Husk på, at det er farligt" (Keep in mind that it is dangerous). To say you remember a name, leave out "på" (on) and use "at huske" (to remember): "Jeg husker hans navn" (I remember his name).

sentence.da: Du skal **huske på**, at vejen er glat.
sentence.en: You must keep in mind that the road is slippery.

at hvile.explanation: "At hvile" means "to rest", as in taking a break. To say you rest yourself for a moment, add "sig" (yourself): "Jeg hviler mig lidt" (I am resting a bit).

sentence.da: Du bør **hvile** benet i en uge.
sentence.en: You should rest your leg for a week.

at hvile sig.explanation: "At hvile sig" means "to rest". It is "at hvile" (to rest) with "sig" (yourself). To say you relax, use "at slappe af" (to relax): "Jeg slapper af i sofaen" (I relax on the sofa).

sentence.da: Han er træt og vil **hvile sig** lidt.
sentence.en: He is tired and wants to rest a little.

at hviske.explanation: "At hviske" means "to whisper". To say who you whisper to, use "til" (to): "Hun hvisker til sin søster" (She whispers to her sister).

sentence.da: Hun vil **hviske** en hemmelighed i mit øre.
sentence.en: She wants to whisper a secret in my ear.

at hygge sig.explanation: "At hygge sig" means "to have a cozy or nice time". To wish someone that, say: "Hyg dig!" (Have a nice time!) To say who you had it with, use "med" (with): "Jeg hyggede mig med mine venner" (I had a nice time with my friends).

forms.en: to have a cozy / nice time
I have a cozy / nice time
I had a cozy / nice time
I have had a cozy / nice time

sentence.da: Familien vil **hygge sig** ved bålet i aften.
sentence.en: The family wants to have a cozy time by the fire tonight.

at hylde.explanation: "At hylde" means "to celebrate or honor". To say people honor a person: "De hylder vinderen" (They honor the winner). For a birthday or a holiday, use "at fejre" (to celebrate): "Vi fejrer min fødselsdag" (We celebrate my birthday).

sentence.da: Hele byen vil **hylde** holdet, der vandt pokalen.
sentence.en: The whole town wants to honor the team that won the cup.

at hyle.explanation: "At hyle" means "to howl". To say the wind howls: "Vinden hyler om huset" (The wind howls around the house).

sentence.da: Ulve kan **hyle** højt om natten.
sentence.en: Wolves can howl loudly at night.

at hyre.explanation: "At hyre" means "to hire". To say you rent something, use "at leje" (to rent): "Vi lejer en bil" (We rent a car).

sentence.da: Vi skal **hyre** en tømrer til at bygge huset.
sentence.en: We must hire a carpenter to build the house.

at håbe.explanation: "At håbe" means "to hope". To name what you hope for, add "på" (on) before it: "håbe på en gave" (hope for a gift). To say you hope so, say: "Det håber jeg" (I hope so).

sentence.da: Vi må **håbe** på godt vejr i morgen.
sentence.en: We must hope for good weather tomorrow.

at håndtere.explanation: "At håndtere" means "to handle". It is built from "hånd" (hand). To say someone deals with complaints: "Hun håndterer klagerne" (She handles the complaints).

sentence.da: Læreren kan **håndtere** en stor klasse uden problemer.
sentence.en: The teacher can handle a big class without problems.

at hælde.explanation: "At hælde" means "to pour or lean". To say you pour a drink: "Jeg hælder mælk i glasset" (I pour milk into the glass). To say something slopes: "Taget hælder" (The roof slopes).

sentence.da: Du skal **hælde** langsomt, når kanden er fuld.
sentence.en: You have to pour slowly when the pitcher is full.

at hænge.explanation: "At hænge" means "to hang". To say you spend time with friends, use "hænge ud" (hang out): "Vi hænger ud efter skole" (We hang out after school).

sentence.da: Jakken skal **hænge** på knagen.
sentence.en: The jacket should hang on the hook.

at hænge op.explanation: "At hænge op" means "to hang up". When something is hung up, "op" (up) comes after it: "Han hænger jakken op" (He hangs the jacket up). To end a phone call, use "at lægge på" (to hang up): "Hun lagde på" (She hung up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hænge op**, når vaskemaskinen er færdig.
sentence.en: I have to hang up the laundry when the washing machine is done.

at hænge sammen.explanation: "At hænge sammen" means "to make sense or be connected". To say things are linked: "Alt hænger sammen" (Everything is connected). To say a story does not add up: "Historien hænger ikke sammen" (The story does not make sense).

forms.en: it has made sense / been connected

sentence.da: Hans forklaring vil ikke **hænge sammen**.
sentence.en: His explanation will not make sense.

at hævde.explanation: "At hævde" means "to claim". To report what someone says is true: "Han hævder, at han var hjemme" (He claims that he was at home). To report plainly what someone said, use "at sige" (to say): "Han siger, at han var hjemme" (He says that he was at home).

sentence.da: Tyven vil **hævde**, at han ikke var der.
sentence.en: The thief will claim that he was not there.

at hævde sig.explanation: "At hævde sig" means "to assert oneself". It is "at hævde" (to claim) with "sig" (oneself). Without "sig", it means "to claim": "Han hævder, at han er uskyldig" (He claims he is innocent).

related.da: at stå op for sig selv

sentence.da: Den unge spiller vil gerne **hævde sig** på landsholdet.
sentence.en: The young player would like to assert himself on the national team.

at hæve.explanation: "At hæve" means "to raise or withdraw (money)". To say you raise a price: "hæve prisen" (raise the price). To say you raise your voice: "Hun hævede stemmen" (She raised her voice).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **hæve** penge i banken i morgen.
sentence.en: I must withdraw money at the bank tomorrow.

at hæve penge.explanation: "At hæve penge" means "to withdraw money". To say you put money in, use "at sætte penge ind" (to deposit money): "Jeg sætter 500 kroner ind" (I deposit 500 kroner).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **hæve penge**, men banken er lukket.
sentence.en: I want to withdraw money, but the bank is closed.

at hævne.explanation: "At hævne" means "to avenge". It is related to the noun "hævn" (revenge). To say you take revenge yourself, use "at hævne sig" (to take revenge): "Hun hævner sig på ham" (She takes revenge on him).

sentence.da: Han vil **hævne** sin bror, som blev såret.
sentence.en: He wants to avenge his brother, who was hurt.

at høre.explanation: "At høre" means "to hear". To say you have heard news: "Jeg har hørt, at han flytter" (I have heard that he is moving). To listen on purpose, use "at lytte" (to listen): "Jeg lytter til musik" (I listen to music).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **høre** dig.
sentence.en: I cannot hear you.

at høre efter.explanation: "At høre efter" means "to listen". To tell children to pay attention: "Hør efter!" (Listen!) To say you hear a sound, use "at høre" (to hear): "Jeg hører en lyd" (I hear a sound).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **høre efter**, når læreren taler.
sentence.en: The children must listen when the teacher speaks.

at høre fra.explanation: "At høre fra" means "to hear from". To say someone has not contacted you: "Jeg har ikke hørt fra Mette" (I have not heard from Mette). For news about something, use "at høre om" (to hear about): "Jeg hørte om ulykken" (I heard about the accident).

sentence.da: Jeg håber at **høre fra** dig snart.
sentence.en: I hope to hear from you soon.

at høre om.explanation: "At høre om" means "to hear about". To say you learned of an event: "Jeg hørte om branden" (I heard about the fire). To say someone contacted you, use "at høre fra" (to hear from): "Jeg har hørt fra Mette" (I have heard from Mette).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **høre om** din rejse.
sentence.en: I would like to hear about your trip.

at høre til.explanation: "At høre til" means "to belong". To name the place you belong in, add "i" (in) before the place: "Jeg hører til i Aarhus" (I belong in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **høre til** i gruppen.
sentence.en: I would like to belong to the group.

at høste.explanation: "At høste" means "to harvest". It is related to "høst" (autumn, the harvest season). To say someone earns praise: "Hun høster ros" (She reaps praise).

sentence.da: Bonden vil **høste** kornet, når det er modent.
sentence.en: The farmer will harvest the grain when it is ripe.

en hage.explanation: "En hage" means "a chin". To say someone has a double chin, use "en dobbelthage" (a double chin): "Han har dobbelthage" (He has a double chin). It is also the first part of "en hagesmæk" (a bib).

sentence.da: Din **hage** sidder lige under munden.
sentence.en: Your chin is right under the mouth.

en hagesmæk.explanation: "En hagesmæk" means "a bib". The first part is "hage" (chin).

sentence.da: Babyen spiser grød med en **hagesmæk** på.
sentence.en: The baby eats porridge with a bib on.

en haj.explanation: "En haj" means "a shark". To say a person who lends money at very high interest, use "en lånehaj" (a loan shark): "Han skyldte en lånehaj penge" (He owed a loan shark money).

sentence.da: En **haj** har skarpe tænder og bor i havet.
sentence.en: A shark has sharp teeth and lives in the sea.

en hakkebøf.explanation: "En hakkebøf" means "a hamburger steak". It is built from "hakke" (to chop) and "bøf" (steak). In Denmark it is served on a plate with brown gravy, not in a bun.

sentence.da: Til aftensmad fik vi **hakkebøf** med bløde løg og kartofler.
sentence.en: For dinner we had hamburger steak with soft onions and potatoes.

en hal.explanation: "En hal" means "a hall", as in a large room or building for sports. For the hallway inside a home, use "en gang" (a hallway): "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway).

sentence.da: En **hal** er et stort rum med plads til mange.
sentence.en: A hall is a big room with space for many people.

en hale.explanation: "En hale" means "a tail". The word is also part of "en hestehale" (a ponytail), where "hest" means "horse".

sentence.da: Hunden logrer med sin **hale**, når den er glad.
sentence.en: The dog wags its tail when it is happy.

en halmballe.explanation: "En halmballe" means "a straw bale". It is built from "halm" (straw) and "balle" (bale).

sentence.da: En **halmballe** er tør halm, der er presset tæt sammen.
sentence.en: A straw bale is dry straw that is pressed tightly together.

en hals.explanation: "En hals" means "a throat or neck". To say you have a sore throat: "Jeg har ondt i halsen" (I have a sore throat). It is also the first part of "en halskæde" (a necklace), where "kæde" means "chain".

sentence.da: Hun har en smuk kæde om sin **hals**.
sentence.en: She has a pretty chain around her neck.

en halsbetændelse.explanation: "En halsbetændelse" means "a throat infection". It is built from "hals" (throat) and "betændelse" (infection). For a plain sore throat, say "ondt i halsen" (a sore throat): "Jeg har ondt i halsen" (I have a sore throat).

sentence.da: Hun har **halsbetændelse** og må blive hjemme.
sentence.en: She has a throat infection and has to stay home.

en halsedisse.explanation: "En halsedisse" means "a neck warmer". The first part is "hals" (neck).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **halsedisse** på, når det blæser.
sentence.en: I put on a neck warmer when it is windy.

en halskæde.explanation: "En halskæde" means "a necklace". It is built from "hals" (neck) and "kæde" (chain).

sentence.da: Hun har en **halskæde** om halsen.
sentence.en: She has a necklace around her neck.

en halspastil.explanation: "En halspastil" means "a throat lozenge". It is built from "hals" (throat) and "pastil" (lozenge).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **halspastil**, når min hals gør ondt.
sentence.en: I take a throat lozenge when my throat hurts.

en halv time.explanation: "En halv time" means "half an hour". To say how long something takes: "Det tager en halv time" (It takes half an hour). Do not mix it up with the clock time "halv fem" (4:30): "Vi mødes klokken halv fem" (We meet at half past four).

sentence.da: Bussen kommer om **en halv time**.
sentence.en: The bus comes in half an hour.

en halvbror.explanation: "En halvbror" means "a half-brother". It is built from "halv" (half) and "bror" (brother).

sentence.da: Han er min **halvbror**, fordi vi har samme far.
sentence.en: He is my half-brother because we have the same father.

en halvdel.explanation: "En halvdel" means "a half". It is built from "halv" (half) and "del" (part). To say half of a thing, put "halv" before the noun: "en halv pizza" (half a pizza).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser den ene **halvdel** af kagen.
sentence.en: I eat one half of the cake.

en halvleg.explanation: "En halvleg" means "a half (of a game)". To say the first half of a match: "første halvleg" (the first half). For one half of a thing you cut, use "en halvdel" (a half): "en halvdel af kagen" (one half of the cake).

sentence.da: Første **halvleg** sluttede nul-nul, men vi scorede efter pausen.
sentence.en: The first half ended 0-0, but we scored after the break.

en halvsøster.explanation: "En halvsøster" means "a half-sister". It is built from "halv" (half) and "søster" (sister).

sentence.da: Hun er min **halvsøster**, fordi vi har samme mor.
sentence.en: She is my half-sister because we have the same mother.

en halvø.explanation: "En halvø" means "a peninsula". It is built from "halv" (half) and "ø" (island). For land with water on all sides, use "en ø" (an island): "Fyn er en ø" (Funen is an island).

sentence.da: Jylland er en **halvø** og hænger sammen med Tyskland.
sentence.en: Jutland is a peninsula and is joined to Germany.

en hammer.explanation: "En hammer" means "a hammer". To drive in a screw, use "en skruetrækker" (a screwdriver): "Jeg skruer skruen i med en skruetrækker" (I screw the screw in with a screwdriver).

sentence.da: Han slår sømmet i med en **hammer**.
sentence.en: He hits the nail in with a hammer.

en hamster.explanation: "En hamster" means "a hamster". The verb "at hamstre" (to hoard) comes from it: "Han hamstrer mad" (He hoards food).

sentence.da: Min **hamster** sover om dagen og løber om natten.
sentence.en: My hamster sleeps during the day and runs around at night.

en handel.explanation: "En handel" means "a deal". To talk about trading as an activity, leave out "en": "Handel mellem lande er vigtig" (Trade between countries is important).

sentence.da: Det var en god **handel** for os begge.
sentence.en: That was a good deal for both of us.

en handling.explanation: "En handling" means "an action". To talk about the plot of a story: "Filmens handling er enkel" (The plot of the film is simple). Do not mix it up with "en handel" (a deal): "Det var en god handel" (That was a good deal).

sentence.da: Hans **handling** var meget modig.
sentence.en: His action was very brave.

en handske.explanation: "En handske" means "a glove". For a glove with one part for the thumb and one for the other fingers, use "en vante" (a mitten): "Barnet har en vante på" (The child has a mitten on).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **handske** på hånden.
sentence.en: I have a glove on my hand.

en hane.explanation: "En hane" means "a rooster or faucet". To tell someone to turn off the faucet: "Luk for hanen" (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: En **hane** galer tidligt om morgenen.
sentence.en: A rooster crows early in the morning.

en harddisk.explanation: "En harddisk" means "a hard drive". It is built from "hård" (hard) and "disk" (disk).

sentence.da: Min **harddisk** er fuld af gamle billeder.
sentence.en: My hard drive is full of old photos.

en hare.explanation: "En hare" means "a hare". For the animal that people keep as a pet, use "en kanin" (a rabbit): "Vi har en kanin i et bur" (We have a rabbit in a cage).

sentence.da: En **hare** kan løbe meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: A hare can run very fast.

en harmoni.explanation: "En harmoni" means "a harmony". To talk about music: "Tonerne danner en harmoni" (The notes form a harmony).

sentence.da: Familien lever i **harmoni**, og der er sjældent skænderier.
sentence.en: The family lives in harmony, and there are rarely quarrels.

en hasselnød.explanation: "En hasselnød" means "a hazelnut". It is built from "hassel" (hazel) and "nød" (nut). The part "nød" is also in "en pebernød" (a small spice cookie eaten at Christmas), which is a cookie, not a nut.

sentence.da: En **hasselnød** er en lille nød med hård skal.
sentence.en: A hazelnut is a small nut with a hard shell.

en hastighed.explanation: "En hastighed" means "a speed". To state how fast something goes: "Hastigheden er 50 kilometer i timen" (The speed is 50 kilometers per hour). The word "fart" (speed) means the same: "høj fart" (high speed).

sentence.da: Du kører med for høj **hastighed**.
sentence.en: You are driving at too high a speed.

en hat.explanation: "En hat" means "a hat". For a warm knitted cap, use "en hue" (a knitted cap): "Om vinteren har jeg en hue på" (In winter I wear a knitted cap). For a cap with a peak, use "en kasket" (a cap): "Han har en kasket på" (He is wearing a cap).

sentence.da: Hun har en stor **hat** på hovedet.
sentence.en: She has a big hat on her head.

en have.explanation: "En have" means "a garden". To say you work in the garden: "Jeg arbejder i haven" (I work in the garden). Do not mix it up with "at have" (to have), which is spelled the same: "Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe" (I would like to have a cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Vi har en **have** med blomster og træer.
sentence.en: We have a garden with flowers and trees.

en havefest.explanation: "En havefest" means "a garden party". It is built from "have" (garden) and "fest" (party).

sentence.da: Til vores **havefest** sidder vi ude og griller.
sentence.en: At our garden party, we sit outside and grill.

en haveslange.explanation: "En haveslange" means "a garden hose". It is built from "have" (garden) and "slange" (hose). The word "slange" also means "snake": "Slangen bed ham" (The snake bit him).

sentence.da: Han vasker bilen med en **haveslange**.
sentence.en: He washes the car with a garden hose.

en havestol.explanation: "En havestol" means "a garden chair". It is built from "have" (garden) and "stol" (chair). The part "have" is also in "en haveslange" (a garden hose) and "en havefest" (a garden party).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i en **havestol** og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: I sit in a garden chair and drink coffee.

en havfrue.explanation: "En havfrue" means "a mermaid". It is built from "hav" (sea) and "frue" (lady).

sentence.da: I eventyret har en **havfrue** en fiskehale i stedet for ben.
sentence.en: In the story, a mermaid has a fish tail instead of legs.

en havn.explanation: "En havn" means "a harbor or port". To say a ship arrives: "Skibet sejler ind i havnen" (The ship sails into the harbor). The word is also the first part of "en havnebus" (a harbor bus).

sentence.da: Der er mange både i en lille **havn**.
sentence.en: There are many boats in a small harbor.

en havnebus.explanation: "En havnebus" means "a harbor bus". It is built from "havn" (harbor) and "bus" (bus).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **havnebus** over vandet, og det tager ti minutter.
sentence.en: We take a harbor bus across the water, and it takes ten minutes.

en havnepromenade.explanation: "En havnepromenade" means "a harbor promenade". It is built from "havn" (harbor) and "promenade" (the same word as in English).

sentence.da: Der ligger caféer og isbarer langs den nye **havnepromenade**.
sentence.en: There are cafés and ice cream bars along the new harbor promenade.

en hede.explanation: "En hede" means "a heath". In Denmark, large heaths are in western Jutland. The word is also in "en hedebølge" (a heat wave), where "hede" means "heat".

sentence.da: På en **hede** er jorden sandet, og der vokser næsten ingen træer.
sentence.en: On a heath the soil is sandy, and almost no trees grow.

en hedebølge.explanation: "En hedebølge" means "a heat wave". It is built from "hede" (heat) and "bølge" (wave). The same pattern gives "en kuldebølge" (a cold spell): "Vi får en kuldebølge i næste uge" (We get a cold spell next week).

sentence.da: Under en **hedebølge** er det næsten for varmt til at sove.
sentence.en: During a heat wave it is almost too hot to sleep.

en heks.explanation: "En heks" means "a witch". It is rude to call a woman this in anger: "Din gamle heks!" (You old witch!) The word is also in "en heksejagt" (a witch hunt).

sentence.da: Børnene var bange for den onde **heks**.
sentence.en: The children were afraid of the evil witch.

en helhed.explanation: "En helhed" means "a whole". It is built from "hel" (whole) and "-hed" (-ness). To say you read the entire book: "Vi har læst bogen i sin helhed" (We have read the entire book).

sentence.da: Delene passer sammen, og de danner en **helhed**.
sentence.en: The pieces fit together, and they form a whole.

en helikopter.explanation: "En helikopter" means "a helicopter". Danish spells it with "k" where English has "c". To say how someone travels: "Han kommer med helikopter" (He comes by helicopter).

sentence.da: En **helikopter** har blade og letter lige op i luften.
sentence.en: A helicopter has blades and takes off straight up into the air.

en helligdag.explanation: "En helligdag" means "a public holiday". It is built from "hellig" (holy) and "dag" (day). A shop sign can say "lukket søn- og helligdage" (closed on Sundays and public holidays).

sentence.da: Juledag er en **helligdag**, og vi har fri.
sentence.en: Christmas Day is a public holiday, and we have the day off.

en hemmelighed.explanation: "En hemmelighed" means "a secret". To ask someone to keep a secret, use "holde" (to hold): "Kan du holde en hemmelighed?" (Can you keep a secret?) To describe a plan as secret, use "hemmelig" (secret): "en hemmelig plan" (a secret plan).

sentence.da: Det er en **hemmelighed**, og ingen må vide det.
sentence.en: It is a secret, and nobody may know.

en hensigt.explanation: "En hensigt" means "an intention". To say you intend to do something: "Jeg har til hensigt at flytte" (I intend to move). This phrase is formal. For everyday talk, use "at ville" (to want): "Jeg vil flytte" (I want to move).

sentence.da: Min **hensigt** var ikke at såre dig.
sentence.en: My intention was not to hurt you.

en henvendelse.explanation: "En henvendelse" means "an inquiry". It comes from the verb "at henvende sig" (to get in touch). To thank someone for getting in touch, customer service says: "Tak for din henvendelse" (Thank you for contacting us).

sentence.da: Vi besvarer din **henvendelse** inden for to hverdage.
sentence.en: We will answer your inquiry within two working days.

en henvisning.explanation: "En henvisning" means "a referral or reference". It comes from the verb "at henvise" (to refer). To say the doctor sends you on: "Lægen skriver en henvisning" (The doctor writes a referral). To say a text points to a source: "Der er en henvisning til kilden nederst" (There is a reference to the source at the bottom).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en **henvisning** fra lægen for at komme på sygehuset.
sentence.en: You need a referral from the doctor to get into the hospital.

en herre.explanation: "En herre" means "a gentleman or lord". To mark the men's restroom, a sign says "Herrer" (Men). Men's clothes are "herretøj" (menswear).

sentence.da: Den høje **herre** dér venter på dig.
sentence.en: That tall gentleman over there is waiting for you.

en hersker.explanation: "En hersker" means "a ruler", as in a person who governs a country. It comes from the verb "at herske" (to rule). To say someone rules a country: "Han hersker over landet" (He rules over the country).

sentence.da: Den, der styrer hele landet alene, er en **hersker**.
sentence.en: The one who rules the whole country alone is a ruler.

en hest.explanation: "En hest" means "a horse". To say you ride: "Hun rider på en hest" (She rides a horse). The word is also the first part of "en hestehale" (a ponytail).

sentence.da: En **hest** spiser græs og løber hurtigt.
sentence.en: A horse eats grass and runs fast.

en hestehale.explanation: "En hestehale" means "a ponytail". It is built from "hest" (horse) and "hale" (tail). To say you tie your hair up: "Jeg binder håret i en hestehale" (I tie my hair in a ponytail).

sentence.da: Hun har samlet håret i en høj **hestehale**.
sentence.en: She has gathered her hair in a high ponytail.

en hilsen.explanation: "En hilsen" means "a greeting". To end a letter or email, write "Venlig hilsen" (Kind regards). To pass on hello to someone: "Mange hilsner til din mor" (Best wishes to your mother).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **hilsen** fra Danmark.
sentence.en: I'm sending you a greeting from Denmark.

en himmel.explanation: "En himmel" means "a sky". To say what the sky looks like, use the form "himlen" (the sky): "Himlen er grå" (The sky is gray). The word is also in "en himmelseng" (a canopy bed).

sentence.da: Der er mange stjerner på en mørk **himmel**.
sentence.en: There are many stars in a dark sky.

en hindbærsnitte.explanation: "En hindbærsnitte" means "a raspberry slice (pastry)". It is built from "hindbær" (raspberry) and "snitte" (slice). In Denmark, bakeries sell it.

sentence.da: Til kaffen fik vi en **hindbærsnitte** med syltetøj og glasur.
sentence.en: With the coffee we had a raspberry slice with jam and icing.

en hindring.explanation: "En hindring" means "an obstacle". It comes from the verb "at hindre" (to prevent). To say something stops you, even something you cannot touch: "Frygt kan være en hindring" (Fear can be an obstacle).

sentence.da: Manglende sprogkundskaber kan være en stor **hindring** i et nyt job.
sentence.en: Missing language skills can be a big obstacle in a new job.

en hingst.explanation: "En hingst" means "a stallion". For a female horse, use "en hoppe" (a mare): "Hoppen står på marken" (The mare is standing in the field).

sentence.da: En **hingst** bruges til avl, så der kommer nye heste.
sentence.en: A stallion is used for breeding, so new horses are born.

en historie.explanation: "En historie" means "a story or history". To say someone tells a story: "Fortæl en historie" (Tell a story). To talk about the past of a country: "Danmarks historie" (the history of Denmark).

sentence.da: Han fortæller en sjov **historie**.
sentence.en: He tells a funny story.

en historiebog.explanation: "En historiebog" means "a history book". It is built from "historie" (history) and "en bog" (a book). The word "historie" also means "story": "en historie om en prins" (a story about a prince).

sentence.da: I vores **historiebog** læser vi om vikingerne.
sentence.en: In our history book, we read about the Vikings.

en historiker.explanation: "En historiker" means "a historian". It comes from "historie" (history). To say someone's job, leave out "en": "Hun er historiker" (She is a historian).

sentence.da: En **historiker** læser gamle breve for at forstå fortiden.
sentence.en: A historian reads old letters to understand the past.

en hjelm.explanation: "En hjelm" means "a helmet". To tell someone to put it on: "Tag din hjelm på" (Put your helmet on).

sentence.da: Børn skal have **hjelm** på, når de cykler.
sentence.en: Children must wear a helmet when they bike.

en hjemmeopgave.explanation: "En hjemmeopgave" means "a homework assignment". It is built from "hjemme" (at home) and "opgave" (task). For the daily homework from school, use "lektier" (homework): "Jeg laver mine lektier" (I do my homework).

sentence.da: Læreren gav klassen en **hjemmeopgave** om Danmarks historie.
sentence.en: The teacher gave the class a homework assignment about Denmark's history.

en hjemmeside.explanation: "En hjemmeside" means "a website". It is built from "hjemme" (home) and "side" (page). Do not mix up "hjemme" (at home) and "hjem" (toward home): "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home) and "Jeg går hjem" (I am going home).

sentence.da: Du kan se åbningstiderne på butikkens **hjemmeside**.
sentence.en: You can see the opening hours on the shop's website.

en hjemmesko.explanation: "En hjemmesko" means "a slipper". It is built from "hjemme" (at home) and "sko" (shoe). To talk about two slippers: "et par hjemmesko" (a pair of slippers).

sentence.da: Jeg har varme **hjemmesko** på i huset.
sentence.en: I am wearing warm slippers in the house.

en hjemrejse.explanation: "En hjemrejse" means "a return trip". It is built from "hjem" (home) and "rejse" (trip). The word "rejse" is also a verb: "at rejse hjem" (to travel home).

sentence.da: Efter ferien starter vores **hjemrejse** fra Spanien.
sentence.en: After the vacation, our trip home starts from Spain.

en hjerne.explanation: "En hjerne" means "a brain". To tell someone to think: "Brug hjernen!" (Use your brain!) The word is also the first part of "hjernerystelse" (concussion), literally "brain shaking".

sentence.da: Din **hjerne** sidder inde i hovedet.
sentence.en: Your brain sits inside the head.

en hjernerystelse.explanation: "En hjernerystelse" means "a concussion". It is built from "hjerne" (brain) and "rystelse" (shaking). To say someone got one: "Han fik en hjernerystelse i går" (He got a concussion yesterday).

sentence.da: En **hjernerystelse** kommer af et hårdt slag mod hovedet.
sentence.en: A concussion comes from a hard blow to the head.

en hjort.explanation: "En hjort" means "a deer". For a smaller deer, use "et rådyr" (a roe deer): "Et rådyr står ved skovkanten" (A roe deer is standing at the edge of the forest).

sentence.da: Vi så en **hjort** med et stort gevir.
sentence.en: We saw a deer with big antlers.

en hobby.explanation: "En hobby" means "a hobby". To ask someone about it: "Hvad er din hobby?" (What is your hobby?)

sentence.da: Min **hobby** er at male billeder.
sentence.en: My hobby is painting pictures.

en hofte.explanation: "En hofte" means "a hip". To say your hip hurts: "Jeg har ondt i hoften" (My hip hurts). To say someone had a hip replacement: "Hun har fået en ny hofte" (She has got a new hip).

sentence.da: Din **hofte** sidder mellem taljen og låret.
sentence.en: Your hip sits between the waist and the thigh.

en holdbarhedsdato.explanation: "En holdbarhedsdato" means "a best-before date". It is built from "holdbarhed" (shelf life) and "dato" (date). To say the date has passed: "Holdbarhedsdatoen er overskredet" (The best-before date has passed).

sentence.da: Jeg tjekker altid mælkens **holdbarhedsdato**.
sentence.en: I always check the milk's best-before date.

en holdkammerat.explanation: "En holdkammerat" means "a teammate". It is built from "et hold" (a team) and "en kammerat" (a buddy). The part "kammerat" also builds "en legekammerat" (a playmate).

sentence.da: Min **holdkammerat** og jeg spiller på samme hold.
sentence.en: My teammate and I play on the same team.

en holdning.explanation: "En holdning" means "an attitude". A very common phrase is "at have en holdning til noget" (to have a view on something). When you talk about how someone stands or sits, it means "posture": "Han har en god holdning" (He has good posture).

sentence.da: Hun har en klar **holdning** til, hvordan skolen skal drives.
sentence.en: She has a clear view on how the school should be run.

en honningkage.explanation: "En honningkage" means "a honey cake or gingerbread". It is built from "honning" (honey) and "en kage" (a cake). The part "kage" also builds "en småkage" (a cookie), which is literally "a small cake".

sentence.da: Vi bager en **honningkage** med honning og kanel.
sentence.en: We bake a honey cake with honey and cinnamon.

en hoppe.explanation: "En hoppe" means "a mare". Do not mix it up with "at hoppe" (to jump), which is spelled the same. To say a horse jumps, use the verb: "Hesten hopper over hegnet" (The horse jumps over the fence).

sentence.da: Når en **hoppe** får et føl, bliver hun mor.
sentence.en: When a mare has a foal, she becomes a mother.

en horisont.explanation: "En horisont" means "a horizon". A very common phrase is "at udvide sin horisont" (to broaden your horizons).

sentence.da: En **horisont** er den linje, hvor himlen møder havet.
sentence.en: A horizon is the line where the sky meets the sea.

en hoste.explanation: "En hoste" means "a cough". A very common phrase is "en slem hoste" (a bad cough): "Jeg har en slem hoste" (I have a bad cough).

sentence.da: Med en **hoste** er det svært at sove.
sentence.en: With a cough, it is hard to sleep.

en hostesaft.explanation: "En hostesaft" means "a cough syrup". It is built from "en hoste" (a cough) and "saft" (juice). The part "saft" also builds "æblesaft" (apple juice).

sentence.da: Jeg tog en skefuld **hostesaft** mod min hoste.
sentence.en: I took a spoonful of cough syrup for my cough.

en hotdog.explanation: "En hotdog" means "a hot dog". Do not mix it up with "en pølse" (a sausage), which is only the sausage without the bun. To ask for only the sausage, say: "En pølse, tak" (A sausage, please).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **hotdog** med ketchup og sennep.
sentence.en: I eat a hot dog with ketchup and mustard.

en hov.explanation: "En hov" means "a hoof". Do not mix it up with "en klov" (a cloven hoof), the split hoof of a cow. To talk about a cow, use the word "klov": "Koens klov er delt i to" (The cow's hoof is split in two).

sentence.da: Hesten har en hård **hov** på hver fod.
sentence.en: The horse has a hard hoof on each foot.

en hovedbanegård.explanation: "En hovedbanegård" means "a central station". It is built from "hoved" (main), "en bane" (a railway) and "en gård" (a yard). In Copenhagen, the central station is written "København H", where the H stands for "hovedbanegård".

sentence.da: København har en stor **hovedbanegård**.
sentence.en: Copenhagen has a big central station.

en hoveddør.explanation: "En hoveddør" means "a front door". It is built from "hoved" (main) and "en dør" (a door). The part "hoved" also means "main" in "en hovedvej" (a main road).

sentence.da: Vores **hoveddør** vender ud mod gaden.
sentence.en: Our front door faces the street.

en hovedgade.explanation: "En hovedgade" means "a main street". It is built from "hoved" (main) and "en gade" (a street). To say where a shop is, use "på" (on): "Bageren ligger på hovedgaden" (The bakery is on the main street).

sentence.da: Der er mange butikker og caféer i byens **hovedgade**.
sentence.en: There are many stores and cafés on the town's main street.

en hovedingrediens.explanation: "En hovedingrediens" means "a main ingredient". It is built from "hoved" (main) and "en ingrediens" (an ingredient). The part "hoved" also appears in "en hovedret" (a main course).

sentence.da: Æg er en **hovedingrediens** i pandekager, sammen med mel og mælk.
sentence.en: Eggs are a main ingredient in pancakes, together with flour and milk.

en hovedperson.explanation: "En hovedperson" means "a main character". It is built from "hoved" (main) and "en person" (a person). To say an actor plays the lead, use "en hovedrolle" (a leading role): "Hun spiller hovedrollen" (She plays the lead).

sentence.da: Hun er **hovedperson** i filmen, så vi ser hende hele tiden.
sentence.en: She is the main character in the film, so we see her all the time.

en hovedpine.explanation: "En hovedpine" means "a headache". It is built from "et hoved" (a head) and "en pine" (a pain). To say your head hurts, use "ondt" (hurting): "Jeg har ondt i hovedet" (My head hurts).

sentence.da: Jeg har **hovedpine** og tager en pille.
sentence.en: I have a headache and take a pill.

en hovedret.explanation: "En hovedret" means "a main course". It is built from "hoved" (main) and "en ret" (a dish). The word "ret" also appears on menus in "dagens ret" (the dish of the day).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser fisk som **hovedret**.
sentence.en: I eat fish for my main course.

en hovedrolle.explanation: "En hovedrolle" means "a leading role". It is built from "hoved" (main) and "en rolle" (a role). To say an actor plays it, use "at spille" (to play): "Hun spiller hovedrollen" (She plays the lead).

sentence.da: Den unge pige fik en **hovedrolle** i den nye film.
sentence.en: The young girl got a leading role in the new movie.

en hovedstad.explanation: "En hovedstad" means "a capital city". It is built from "et hoved" (a head) and "en stad" (a city), so it is literally a head city. The part "hoved" also means "main", as in "en hovedvej" (a main road).

sentence.da: København er Danmarks **hovedstad**.
sentence.en: Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark.

en hovmester.explanation: "En hovmester" means "a head waiter". To ask for the head waiter in a restaurant, say: "Kan jeg tale med hovmesteren?" (Can I speak to the head waiter?)

sentence.da: En **hovmester** byder gæsterne velkommen og viser dem hen til bordet.
sentence.en: A head waiter welcomes the guests and shows them to the table.

en hr-medarbejder.explanation: "En HR-medarbejder" means "an HR employee". It is built from "HR", "med" (with) and "en arbejder" (a worker). To say a company has hired a new person, use "ansat" (hired): "Vi har ansat en ny medarbejder" (We have hired a new employee).

sentence.da: Vores **HR-medarbejder** hjælper med ansættelser og spørgsmål om løn.
sentence.en: Our HR employee helps with hiring and questions about pay.

en hudlæge.explanation: "En hudlæge" means "a dermatologist". It is built from "en hud" (a skin) and "en læge" (a doctor). The part "hud" also appears in "en hudcreme" (a skin cream).

sentence.da: Jeg har udslæt og skal til **hudlæge**.
sentence.en: I have a rash and am going to the dermatologist.

en hue.explanation: "En hue" means "a beanie". Do not mix it up with "en kasket" (a cap with a peak). To say you take your cap along, use "kasket": "Jeg tager kasketten med i dag" (I am taking my cap along today).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **hue** på hovedet.
sentence.en: I have a warm beanie on my head.

en hugorm.explanation: "En hugorm" means "an adder". The ending "orm" means "worm", as in "en regnorm" (an earthworm). Do not mix it up with "en snog" (a grass snake): "En snog er ikke giftig" (A grass snake is not venomous).

sentence.da: Den eneste giftige slange i Danmark er en **hugorm**.
sentence.en: The only venomous snake in Denmark is an adder.

en hukommelse.explanation: "En hukommelse" means "a memory", as in the ability to remember. To talk about one thing from the past that you remember, use "et minde" (a memory of an event): "Det er et dejligt minde" (That is a lovely memory).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver ting ned, fordi min **hukommelse** er dårlig.
sentence.en: I write things down because my memory is bad.

en hule.explanation: "En hule" means "a cave". To say where a wild animal lives, use it for a den: "Ræven bor i en hule" (The fox lives in a den).

sentence.da: Flagermus sover om dagen i en mørk **hule**.
sentence.en: Bats sleep during the day in a dark cave.

en humlebi.explanation: "En humlebi" means "a bumblebee". The ending "bi" means "bee", as in "en honningbi" (a honeybee).

sentence.da: En **humlebi** er rund og lodden og summer højt mellem blomsterne.
sentence.en: A bumblebee is round and furry and buzzes loudly between the flowers.

en hummer.explanation: "En hummer" means "a lobster". To talk about lobster as food, leave out "en": "Vi bestiller hummer" (We order lobster).

sentence.da: En **hummer** bor i havet og har store klør.
sentence.en: A lobster lives in the sea and has big claws.

en hund.explanation: "En hund" means "a dog". A very common phrase is "at gå tur med hunden" (to take the dog for a walk): "Jeg går tur med hunden" (I take the dog for a walk).

sentence.da: Min **hund** elsker at løbe efter katten.
sentence.en: My dog loves to run after the cat.

en hundeejer.explanation: "En hundeejer" means "a dog owner". It is built from "en hund" (a dog) and "en ejer" (an owner). The part "ejer" also builds "en husejer" (a homeowner).

sentence.da: Som **hundeejer** går jeg lange ture hver dag.
sentence.en: As a dog owner, I take long walks every day.

en hundekurv.explanation: "En hundekurv" means "a dog bed". It is built from "en hund" (a dog) and "en kurv" (a basket). The part "kurv" also builds "en indkøbskurv" (a shopping basket).

sentence.da: Vi har købt en blød **hundekurv** til vores hund.
sentence.en: We have bought a soft dog bed for our dog.

en hundelufter.explanation: "En hundelufter" means "a dog walker". It comes from "at lufte hund" (to walk a dog). To say you are taking your dog out, use "at lufte" (to walk, literally "to air"): "Jeg skal lufte hunden" (I am going to walk the dog).

sentence.da: Vores **hundelufter** henter hunden klokken tolv.
sentence.en: Our dog walker picks up the dog at twelve o'clock.

en hundeskov.explanation: "En hundeskov" means "a dog park". It is built from "en hund" (a dog) and "en skov" (a forest). The part "skov" also builds "en skovtur" (a walk in the forest).

sentence.da: Man må lukke hunden løs i en **hundeskov**.
sentence.en: You may let the dog off the leash in a dog park.

en hushjælp.explanation: "En hushjælp" means "a domestic helper". It is built from "et hus" (a house) and "en hjælp" (a help). The part "hjælp" also appears in "førstehjælp" (first aid).

sentence.da: Vores **hushjælp** gør rent og vasker tøj.
sentence.en: Our domestic helper cleans and does laundry.

en husholdning.explanation: "En husholdning" means "a household". To talk about the daily running of a home, use the word for the work of keeping it going: "Hun styrer husholdningen" (She runs the household).

sentence.da: De har fælles **husholdning** og deler alle udgifterne.
sentence.en: They have a shared household and split all the expenses.

en husmor.explanation: "En husmor" means "a housewife". It is built from "et hus" (a house) and "en mor" (a mother). To say what someone is, leave out "en": "Hun er husmor" (She is a housewife).

sentence.da: En **husmor** passer hjemmet og børnene hele dagen.
sentence.en: A housewife looks after the home and the children all day.

en huspris.explanation: "En huspris" means "a house price". It is built from "et hus" (a house) and "en pris" (a price). To say prices are going up, use "at stige" (to rise): "Huspriserne stiger" (House prices are rising).

sentence.da: En høj **huspris** gør det svært for unge at købe bolig.
sentence.en: A high house price makes it hard for young people to buy a home.

en husregel.explanation: "En husregel" means "a house rule". It is built from "et hus" (a house) and "en regel" (a rule). To say you follow the rules, use "at overholde" (to follow): "Vi overholder husreglerne" (We follow the house rules).

sentence.da: Vores **husregel** er, at man tager skoene af.
sentence.en: Our house rule is that you take your shoes off.

en husstand.explanation: "En husstand" means "a household". A common phrase in official texts is "husstandens samlede indkomst" (the household's total income).

sentence.da: Der bor fire personer i vores **husstand**.
sentence.en: Four people live in our household.

en hustru.explanation: "En hustru" means "a wife". It is a formal word. To introduce your wife in a formal setting, say: "Må jeg præsentere min hustru?" (May I introduce my wife?) To introduce your wife in everyday speech, use "en kone": "Det er min kone" (That is my wife).

sentence.da: Han præsenterede sin **hustru** for gæsterne ved middagen.
sentence.en: He introduced his wife to the guests at dinner.

en hval.explanation: "En hval" means "a whale". Do not mix it up with "en hvalp" (a puppy). To say what a puppy is, use: "En hvalp er en ung hund" (A puppy is a young dog).

sentence.da: En stor **hval** svømmer langt ude i havet.
sentence.en: A big whale swims far out in the sea.

en hvalp.explanation: "En hvalp" means "a puppy". To talk about the young of a fox, use it too: "en rævehvalp" (a fox cub).

sentence.da: En **hvalp** bliver til en stor hund.
sentence.en: A puppy grows into a big dog.

en hvalros.explanation: "En hvalros" means "a walrus". Do not mix it up with "en hval" (a whale). To say which one is bigger, use: "En hval er meget større end en hvalros" (A whale is much bigger than a walrus).

sentence.da: En **hvalros** har lange stødtænder og lever i det kolde Arktis.
sentence.en: A walrus has long tusks and lives in the cold Arctic.

en hveps.explanation: "En hveps" means "a wasp". Do not mix it up with "en bi" (a bee): "En bi laver honning" (A bee makes honey). To say a wasp stung you, use the verb "at stikke" (to sting): "Jeg blev stukket af en hveps" (I was stung by a wasp).

sentence.da: En **hveps** er gul og sort og kan stikke.
sentence.en: A wasp is yellow and black and can sting.

en hverdag.explanation: "En hverdag" means "a weekday or everyday life". To say you do something on weekdays, use "om hverdagen" (on weekdays): "Jeg arbejder om hverdagen" (I work on weekdays). To talk about your daily routine, it means "everyday life": "Hverdagen er travl" (Everyday life is busy).

sentence.da: Lørdag er ikke en **hverdag**, men en weekend.
sentence.en: Saturday is not a weekday, but a weekend.

en hvidvin.explanation: "En hvidvin" means "a white wine". It is built from "hvid" (white) and "en vin" (a wine). To order a bottle, put the drink straight after the word for the bottle: "en flaske hvidvin" (a bottle of white wine).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker et glas **hvidvin** til fisk.
sentence.en: I drink a glass of white wine with fish.

en hyld.explanation: "En hyld" means "an elder tree". Danes make "hyldeblomstsaft" (elderflower cordial) from its flowers. Do not mix it up with "en hylde" (a shelf): "Bogen står på hylden" (The book is on the shelf).

sentence.da: På en **hyld** vokser der hvide blomster, og senere mørke bær.
sentence.en: On an elder tree there grow white flowers, and later dark berries.

en hylde.explanation: "En hylde" means "a shelf". Do not mix it up with "en hyld" (an elder tree): "En hyld har hvide blomster" (An elder tree has white flowers).

sentence.da: Tallerkenerne står på den øverste **hylde**.
sentence.en: The plates are on the top shelf.

en hyldeblomst.explanation: "En hyldeblomst" means "an elderflower". It is built from "en hyld" (an elder tree) and "en blomst" (a flower). Danes make "hyldeblomstsaft" (elderflower cordial) from it.

sentence.da: En **hyldeblomst** er lille og hvid og dufter sødt.
sentence.en: An elderflower is small and white and smells sweet.

en hypotese.explanation: "En hypotese" means "a hypothesis". A very common phrase is "at opstille en hypotese" (to put forward a hypothesis): "Forskeren opstiller en hypotese" (The researcher puts forward a hypothesis).

sentence.da: Vi tester vores **hypotese** med et lille forsøg.
sentence.en: We test our hypothesis with a small experiment.

en hytte.explanation: "En hytte" means "a cabin". To talk about a holiday home by the coast, use "et sommerhus" (a summer house): "Vi har et sommerhus ved havet" (We have a summer house by the sea).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lille **hytte** i skoven.
sentence.en: We live in a small cabin in the forest.

en hånd.explanation: "En hånd" means "a hand". To say two people shake hands, use "at give hånd" (literally, "to give hand"): "Vi giver hinanden hånd" (We shake hands). The plural is spelled "hænder", with æ.

sentence.da: Jeg har fem fingre på hver **hånd**.
sentence.en: I have five fingers on each hand.

en håndbevægelse.explanation: "En håndbevægelse" means "a hand gesture". It is built from "en hånd" (a hand) and "en bevægelse" (a movement). The part "bevægelse" also builds "en armbevægelse" (an arm movement).

sentence.da: Med en **håndbevægelse** bad han os om at være stille.
sentence.en: With a hand gesture he asked us to be quiet.

en håndflade.explanation: "En håndflade" means "a palm". It is built from "en hånd" (a hand) and "en flade" (a flat surface).

sentence.da: Hun læste linjerne i min **håndflade**.
sentence.en: She read the lines in my palm.

en håndfuld.explanation: "En håndfuld" means "a handful". To say how much fits in one hand, put the thing after it: "en håndfuld nødder" (a handful of nuts). To say a very small number of people, it also means "a handful": "Der var kun en håndfuld mennesker" (Only a handful of people were there).

sentence.da: Hun tog en **håndfuld** mandler fra skålen.
sentence.en: She took a handful of almonds from the bowl.

en håndtaske.explanation: "En håndtaske" means "a handbag". It is built from "en hånd" (a hand) and "en taske" (a bag). The part "taske" also builds "en skoletaske" (a school bag).

sentence.da: Hun har sin telefon og pung i sin **håndtaske**.
sentence.en: She has her phone and wallet in her handbag.

en håndvask.explanation: "En håndvask" means "a sink". It is built from "en hånd" (a hand) and "en vask" (a wash). To remind people to wash their hands, use "håndvask" for the act of washing: "Husk håndvask!" (Remember to wash your hands!)

sentence.da: Der er en **håndvask** ved siden af toilettet.
sentence.en: There is a sink next to the toilet.

en håndvægt.explanation: "En håndvægt" means "a dumbbell". It is built from "en hånd" (a hand) and "en vægt" (a weight). The part "vægt" also means "a scale": "Jeg står på vægten" (I am standing on the scale).

sentence.da: Man træner armene med en **håndvægt**.
sentence.en: You train your arms with a dumbbell.

en håndværker.explanation: "En håndværker" means "a tradesperson". It comes from "et håndværk" (a trade or craft). To say you work in a trade, use "et håndværk": "Han har lært et håndværk" (He has learned a trade).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en **håndværker** til at lave taget.
sentence.en: We need a tradesperson to fix the roof.

en hårbørste.explanation: "En hårbørste" means "a hairbrush". It is built from "hår" (hair) and "en børste" (a brush). To say you brush your hair, use the verb "at børste": "Jeg børster mit hår hver morgen" (I brush my hair every morning).

sentence.da: En **hårbørste** er til håret, og en tandbørste er til tænderne.
sentence.en: A hairbrush is for the hair, and a toothbrush is for the teeth.

en hårelastik.explanation: "En hårelastik" means "a hair tie". It is built from "hår" (hair) and "en elastik" (an elastic band). To say you put your hair up, use "at binde op" (to tie up): "Jeg binder håret op" (I tie my hair up).

sentence.da: Jeg samler håret med en **hårelastik**.
sentence.en: I tie my hair back with a hair tie.

en hårfarve.explanation: "En hårfarve" means "a hair color". It is built from "hår" (hair) and "en farve" (a color). To talk about the dye you buy, use it too: "Hun har købt en ny hårfarve" (She has bought a new hair dye).

sentence.da: Min **hårfarve** er brun, men min søsters er blond.
sentence.en: My hair color is brown, but my sister's is blond.

en hæftemaskine.explanation: "En hæftemaskine" means "a stapler". It is built from "at hæfte" (to staple) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you staple pages, use the verb: "Jeg hæfter siderne sammen" (I staple the pages together).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **hæftemaskine** til at sætte papirerne sammen.
sentence.en: I use a stapler to put the papers together.

en hæk.explanation: "En hæk" means "a hedge". A very common phrase is "at klippe hækken" (to trim the hedge): "Jeg klipper hækken i weekenden" (I trim the hedge on the weekend).

sentence.da: Vores nabo har en høj **hæk** rundt om haven.
sentence.en: Our neighbor has a tall hedge around the garden.

en hæl.explanation: "En hæl" means "a heel", as in the back of the foot. To talk about the raised back part of a shoe, it means "heel" too: "Hun har sko med høje hæle" (She has shoes with high heels).

sentence.da: Min **hæl** er bag på foden.
sentence.en: My heel is at the back of the foot.

en hændelse.explanation: "En hændelse" means "an incident". It comes from the verb "at hænde" (to happen). To say something happened, use the verb: "Der hændte noget i går" (Something happened yesterday).

sentence.da: Politiet skriver en rapport om den **hændelse**, der skete i går.
sentence.en: The police write a report about the incident that happened yesterday.

en hængekøje.explanation: "En hængekøje" means "a hammock". It is built from "at hænge" (to hang) and "en køje" (a bunk). The part "køje" also builds "en køjeseng" (a bunk bed).

sentence.da: Vi hænger en **hængekøje** op mellem to træer i haven.
sentence.en: We hang a hammock between two trees in the garden.

en hær.explanation: "En hær" means "an army". In Denmark, "Hæren" is the army, next to "Søværnet" (the navy) and "Flyvevåbnet" (the air force).

sentence.da: Landets **hær** består af soldater og officerer.
